narrative.overview:
On an ECM sleeve, quiet is the field the music sits on. Audio Splitter draws a source file that way: every gap is one sea-mist field in every view, tracks are graphite waveforms and slate blocks laid on it, and a split reads as a rust line you can see before you read a number. The world refuses the dark audio editor with a bright blue waveform, the studio-gear look, the grey screen with one accent, decoration that competes with the waveforms, and dense tiny technical type.

By day the ground is fog and the panels are sleeve white; by night the ground is slate-black, the panels a step lighter and the gaps deep-sea. Ink and audio are graphite, inverted at night. Slate is the colour of what you press, of the header band and of the track blocks. Rust marks splits and the silence threshold, and nothing else. A `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` carries the theme in effect; how it is set is in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md#the-theme).

The waveforms and the loudness curve are the content, so the chrome is quiet: one face, two small radii, flat colour, and controls that carry state through ink and border rather than colour.

rules.name: The Rust Rule
rules.body: Rust marks a split, the silence threshold, a destructive action or an invalid value, and nothing else: not hover, not selection, not links, not emphasis, not a progress fill, not the brand mark. A split item in the track strip is a split, so it takes rust when it is hovered, focused or selected.

rules.name: The Slate Fill Rule
rules.body: Only a pressable thing is a slate fill. Panels, tooltips, sliders and progress are never slate.

rules.name: The Silence Rule
rules.body: A gap is one sea-mist field in every view, never a grey, never a second colour.

rules.name: The Graphite Rule
rules.body: Audio is drawn in graphite. A waveform or curve is never coloured, never blue, never rust. A track block is slate, as the one block-shaped thing.

rules.name: The Twelve-Pixel Floor
rules.body: Nothing is set below 12 px, and nothing is uppercased or letter-spaced to look technical.

rules.name: The Full-Strength Text Rule
rules.body: Text hierarchy comes from size, weight and the `muted` token, never from opacity on text.

rules.name: The Flat Sleeve Rule
rules.body: No `box-shadow`, no `drop-shadow`, no gradient, no blur, no translucency over content. If something needs to stand apart, it gets the surface colour, a hairline, or ground around it.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 3 px for anything you press or type into, 4 px for a panel, fully round only for tracks, thumbs, bars and chips. No other radius.

rules.name: The Land Rule
rules.body: A gap is always drawn as land, never as waveform, and never narrower than 12 px in a whole-file view.

rules.name: The Shared Token Rule
rules.body: Canvas code never hard-codes a colour; it reads the `--color-…` variables, so canvases and kit change theme together.

rules.name: The Ink Focus Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is always a 2 px outline at 2 px offset in the ink of its ground (`ink`, `on-band` on the header band, `on-track` on a track block, `split` on an invalid field).

dos: **Do** take every colour, radius and text size from a token; add a token before a one-off value.
donts: **Don't** read `prefers-color-scheme` in CSS, the kit or a canvas. Dark values key on `[data-theme='dark']`, which only the theme module and the head script in `index.html` set.
